title: From Egocentric Human Video to Robot Manipulation in the Era of Embodied Intelligence
comment: 39 pages, 10 figures. Project page: this https URL
summary: Egocentric human video (EHV) records close-range hand-object interaction (HOI) and the temporal structure of everyday activities, offering a potentially scalable source of experience for robot manipulation. Using this experience for robot control requires recovering useful supervision without recorded robot actions and accounting for differences in morphology, viewpoint, and action space. We define Ego2Robot learning as the process of learning or adapting robot manipulation policies from EHV, organized into four learning paradigms: explicit embodiment transfer, explicit action and task supervision, egocentric video representation pretraining, and latent action and dynamics modeling. The four paradigms differ in what they derive from human video: robot-format demonstrations, interpretable supervision, visual representations, or predictive models of actions and dynamics. For each paradigm, we trace what EHV information is extracted, how robot policies use it, and when the additional data is required. Besides, we review the benchmark datasets that cover EHV, robot demonstrations, and synthetic and simulated resources. This paper links EHV data's contribution to the task information preserved and the robot-specific grounding used during training or deployment. Finally, we identify challenges in physical feasibility, agent coordination, in-context adaptation, controlled evaluation, and predictive control.

title: Few-Shot Residual Adaptation of Pretrained Latent World Models
summary: Pretrained latent world models can support visual planning and control, but their predictions may fail when physical dynamics change at deployment. We study whether such models can adapt from only a few interactions without modifying their pretrained weights or identifying the changed physical parameters. We introduce a few-shot residual adaptation approach that learns self-supervised corrections from latent prediction errors. The corrections are applied both inside the latent predictor and directly to its predicted latent state, while the pretrained world model remains frozen. We evaluate the approach in simulation and on a real robot under center-of-mass and friction shifts. These changes reduce the success of the frozen model to near zero. Using three interaction episodes for adaptation, our dual-site approach recovers 90\% success under the center-of-mass shift and 100\% under the modified friction on the real robot. Ablations show that correcting both locations outperforms single-site adaptation. Our diagnostics further suggest that much of the learned correction reduces a general prediction mismatch, while successful control also depends on shift-specific information captured during adaptation.

AI.motivation: 预训练潜世界模型可用于视觉规划与控制，但部署时物理动力学改变会使预测失败。作者要研究：能否在不修改预训练权重、也不识别具体变化物理参数的情况下，仅凭少量交互完成适应。

title: RoboACE: Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robot Self-Improvement
comment: 13 pages, 5 figures
summary: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. Starting from a compact set of LIBERO practice conditions, the resulting frozen deployment outperforms the evaluated controllers and agent systems across four LIBERO-family panels. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 74.0% success, exceeding the initial deployment by 15.0 percentage points and direct execution by its VLA controller by 13.5 points. Case studies document changes to evidence-guided practice selection, drawer-skill grounding, and controller intervention.

AI.tldr: RoboACE 让"选什么练习"与"执行能力修订"围绕冻结基础模型交替共演化，从少量 LIBERO 练习条件出发，使最终冻结部署在 LIBERO-PRO 上达到 74.0% 成功率。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出：机器人代理虽能借助执行反馈改进可复用技能、规划流程与恢复策略，但固定的练习来源不会改变"搜索新弱点"的方式；有用的练习取决于代理当前能力，因此挑选练习的程序本身也必须可修订。
AI.method: 输入是执行反馈与累积的能力证据。方法把系统拆成两个 harness：curriculum harness 依据累积能力证据提出有信息量的挑战，execution harness 用可复用的修订来扩展执行能力。两者交替更新，更新一侧时固定另一侧；被接纳的挑战被冻结为固定快照，用于比较不同执行修订的优劣。基础模型保持冻结。输出是一个冻结部署，以及被共同演化的课程与执行修订。

title: Joint-State Inference for Autonomous Excavators Using Cab-View Vision-Control Fusion
summary: Reliable state feedback of excavator front-end mechanisms is essential for autonomous excavation, yet retrofitting existing machines with dedicated joint sensors, external cameras, or visual markers can increase deployment and maintenance burdens. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous excavation framework for continuous inference of excavator joint states using onboard visual observations and control-related temporal information. The framework encodes structural cues from the current cab-view image, models short-term motion trends from historical joystick commands, and introduces a rolling state buffer for the bucket joint to preserve temporal continuity under severe occlusion. Mechanical joint-range constraints are incorporated into the learning objective to suppress infeasible estimates. The current cab-view image and inferred states are supplied to an Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT)-based control policy for online action generation. Experiments in an AGX Dynamics for Unity simulation environment under diverse operating conditions evaluate joint-state inference and end-to-end task execution. Across 20 autonomous excavation trials, the framework achieved a 95% task-completion rate, with an average joint-state-inference-and-control latency of 10.11 ms per step. The bucket-joint inference achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.965 degrees. These results demonstrate a sensor-light and computationally efficient joint-state-inference approach that can support closed-loop autonomous excavation with reduced dependence on additional sensing infrastructure.

title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control
summary: Predicting long action chunks, often spanning dozens of timesteps, has become a key ingredient in increasingly capable robot policies. In this paper, we find that adapting these long-chunk policies with existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods can require many online samples due to the high dimensionality of the action chunks being optimized, making such adaptation impractical in real-world scenarios where interaction data are costly to collect. Our key insight is to shift adaptation from optimizing actions to optimizing how long to execute each predicted action chunk. This keeps the adaptation space low-dimensional while its expressivity grows with the chunk size. We thus introduce Execution at the Right Length (ExRL), a simple approach which augments the base policy with a lightweight adapter that predicts the execution length of each chunk and is trained using off-policy RL algorithms. Across simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks, ExRL enables sample-efficient adaptation of a diverse range of long-chunk policies with minimal task-specific hyperparameter tuning.

AI.tldr: 长动作块策略用现有 RL 做在线适配需要大量样本，因为要优化的动作块维度很高。ExRL 把适配对象从"动作"改为"每个块执行多长时间"，用一个轻量适配器加离策略 RL 学习执行长度；作者称在仿真基准和真机机器人任务上实现了样本高效适配，但摘要未报告任何数值。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出：预测跨数十个时间步的长动作块已成为更强机器人策略的关键成分，但用现有强化学习方法适配这类策略时，由于被优化的动作块维度高，往往需要很多在线样本；而在真机场景中交互数据采集成本高昂，这种适配变得不实用。
AI.method: 输入是基础策略已预测出的动作块（可跨数十个时间步）。ExRL 不改动块内动作，而是在基础策略上增加一个轻量适配器，输出每个块的"执行长度"，即这个块要执行多久。训练用离策略（off-policy）RL 算法完成。其设计意图是：把适配的搜索空间从高维动作块压缩成低维的长度决策，而表达力随块尺寸增大而增长。输出是每个预测块的执行长度，据此决定何时切换到下一个块。
AI.result: 作者声称在仿真基准与真实机器人任务上，ExRL 能让多种长块策略实现样本高效的适配，并且只需极少任务特定超参数调优。摘要未报告任何数值：没有样本数、成功率、对比基线名称、任务数量或硬件信息，因此该"样本高效"只是作者的定性主张，摘要中不存在可核验的量化增益（既无法区分相对百分比提升与百分点提升）。

title: DeRep: Learning Depth Representations for End-to-End Navigation in Cluttered Environments
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures
summary: End-to-end navigation in cluttered environments relies on compact visual representations to support collision avoidance and goal-directed motion. Existing methods typically learn these representations jointly with the policy or through observation reconstruction, which does not explicitly specify what information the representation should preserve. Moreover, they are usually evaluated with a single downstream policy learner, although the benefit of a representation may depend on how the policy is learned. It therefore remains unclear how different representation-learning objectives affect downstream navigation performance and robustness. This work proposes DeRep, a navigation-oriented representation-learning method that combines local bird's-eye-view reachability supervision with depth reconstruction. To compare representation objectives under controlled conditions, we pretrain encoders with a common architecture and freeze them during downstream learning. We evaluate the representations using a linear policy probe, flow-matching imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with PPO. DeRep achieves the lowest linear policy probe prediction error and outperforms reconstruction alone across all six tested PPO conditions. In imitation learning, both reachability-based objectives achieve higher mean success rates than reconstruction alone, with similar mean success rates between the reachability-only and joint objectives. These results demonstrate consistent benefits of incorporating reachability supervision into depth representation pretraining across different downstream learning methods and evaluation conditions. We further deploy the PPO policy with the frozen DeRep encoder in Gazebo and on a physical quadrotor without fine-tuning, demonstrating its capability for zero-shot sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer.

title: CIALLO: Learning Shared Intent Representations for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation
summary: Robot demonstrations contain reusable manipulation knowledge, but transferring this knowledge across embodiments requires representations that bridge differences in control interfaces. Action reconstruction alone does not ensure that similar behaviors across robots share a representation. To address this gap, we introduce CIALLO, an action codec that aligns actions, visual changes, and observation-grounded language in a shared space of short-horizon behavioral intent. An embodiment-conditioned decoder maps this intent back to robot-specific actions, allowing a shared representation to support different control interfaces. After pretraining on eight embodiments, CIALLO adapts to a new robot from one recording of at most 10 seconds by updating only its embodiment embeddings. The calibrated codec then remains frozen while a policy learns to predict intent from observations and instructions. We instantiate this policy with Qwen3.5-4B to form Qwen-CIALLO, whose backbone requires no large-scale robot-action pretraining before policy finetuning. With 20 demonstrations per task, Qwen-CIALLO achieves 76.7\% average success across real SO-101 and single-arm Piper robots, compared with 70.0\% for fully finetuned $\pi_0$. In simulation, we additionally finetune the action decoder, achieving 97.3\% success on LIBERO and 52.7\% on RoboTwin 2.0. The LIBERO policy also achieves 80.8\% on LIBERO-Plus without further finetuning. Together, these results support a shared action codec as a transferable control interface that separates embodiment calibration from task learning.

AI.tldr: CIALLO 是一种跨本体动作编解码器，把动作、视觉变化与语言对齐到共享的"短时行为意图"空间；真实机器人上 20 条演示即达 76.7% 平均成功率，高于全量微调 π0 的 70.0%。
AI.motivation: 作者指出：机器人演示含可复用操作知识，但跨本体迁移需要能弥合控制接口差异的表示；仅做动作重建不能保证不同机器人上的相似行为共享同一表示。
AI.method: 输入是多本体机器人演示及其对应的动作、视觉变化和观察基础语言；CIALLO 把它们编码到共享的"短时行为意图"空间，再由**本体条件解码器**把意图映射回各机器人特有的动作。流程分两步：(1) 在八个本体上预训练，迁移到新机器人时只需一段最长 10 秒的录制，且仅更新该本体的嵌入（embodiment embeddings）完成标定；(2) 标定后的编解码器保持冻结，策略只学习从观察与指令预测意图。作者用 Qwen3.5-4B 实例化该策略得到 Qwen-CIALLO，其 backbone 在策略微调前不需要大规模机器人动作预训练。输出是一个可迁移的共享控制接口加上意图预测策略；相对基线的关键改动是把"本体标定"与"任务学习"解耦。

title: ReACT: Reflection-Consistent Modulation and Cross-Load Consistency for Humanoid Velocity Tracking Under Asymmetric Loads
summary: In recent years, humanoid loco-manipulation has progressed to whole-body grasping, lifting, and transport. A basic requirement underlying these tasks is carrying the object to its destination, which depends on the locomotion controller accurately executing velocity commands from the navigation policy. However, carrying an object in one hand introduces a persistent asymmetric upper-body load that can degrade velocity tracking. Persistent tracking biases can accumulate into position and heading deviations, increasing the risk of collisions and navigation failure. To address this problem, we present ReACT, a framework for accurate velocity tracking under asymmetric upper-body loads. Reflection-consistent disturbance modulation uses the estimated wrench to modulate actor features for load compensation while preserving action correspondence under reflected observations. Cross-load tracking consistency training compares loaded and unloaded conditions under the same velocity commands to promote consistent velocity tracking across loading conditions. Simulation experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot show improved velocity tracking and reduced directional bias under varying asymmetric loads. Real-world experiments demonstrate collision-free goal reaching in all 40 tested navigation trials under unilateral hand loads with a fixed mapless navigation policy.

AI.tldr: 单手握物带来的持续非对称上身负载会破坏人形机器人的速度跟踪，并使偏差累积为位置与朝向偏移，增加碰撞和导航失败风险。ReACT 用估计力旋调制 actor 特征做负载补偿，并在相同速度指令下对齐载物与空载的跟踪行为；作者报告 Unitree G1 仿真中速度跟踪改善、方向偏差降低，真机在单侧手部负载下 40 次导航试验全部无碰撞到达。
AI.motivation: 搬运物体的任务要求运动控制器准确执行导航策略下发的速度指令，但单手握持形成持续的非对称上身负载，会削弱速度跟踪；持续的跟踪偏差会累积为位置与朝向偏移，提高碰撞与导航失败的风险。摘要指出这是需要专门解决的问题。

AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的意义在于：把负载感知的扰动调制与跨负载一致性训练放进人形底层控制器，可能减少由底层跟踪偏差传导到导航层的失败。但证据边界明确——仿真结论无量化数字，真机结论仅为作者报告的导航成功率，未给负载质量范围与基线对照，且所有结果均为作者自述、未经独立复核。

title: Robo-MLT: Dual-System Robotic Manipulation for Long-Horizon Medical Laboratory Tasks
comment: 12 pages,7 figures,5 tables,1 algorithm
summary: Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. We evaluate Robo-MLT against four policy baselines and a VLM-based monitor baseline on blood gas analysis and blood sample tube sorting, with 50 nominal configurations per method and 20 sample-removal configurations. Robo-MLT achieves task success rates of 82\% and 70\%, exceeding $\pi_{0.5}$ by 30 and 22 percentage points, respectively. After an operator removes the sample being handled, the system revises the remaining plan and continues processing the other samples. These results indicate that, under the evaluated conditions, explicit workflow monitoring makes long-horizon laboratory manipulation more reliable and recoverable.

AI.tldr: 面向医学实验室长时程操作，Robo-MLT 将显式工作流监控与学习动作生成结合。作者报告在血气分析和血样管分拣上任务成功率为 82% 和 70%，分别超过 π_{0.5} 30 和 22 个百分点。

title: DexSeed: Expanding Human Hand-Object Interactions into Robot Demonstrations for Dexterous Policy Learning

summary: We study how to generate diverse, physically executable robot demonstrations for dexterous vision-language-action (VLA) learning. Existing demonstration-generation methods typically rely on costly teleoperated examples. Meanwhile, human hand--object datasets provide a reusable source, but existing transfer methods mainly reproduce given interactions. Turning these interactions into VLA training data further requires coverage of different objects and manipulation locations, together with executable arm and finger actions, and visual observations. To achieve this, we present DexSeed, a framework for low-cost generation of dexterous robot data from human hand--object interactions. Our key idea is to expand human sequences while preserving their grasps and realizing the resulting motions under arm-tracking dynamics in physics simulation. Specifically, we organize source sequences by grasp mode with shared language descriptions. InteractionMesh-based retargeting and arm trajectory augmentation adapt these sequences to the robot hand, different object geometries, and pick-and-place locations while preserving local hand--object relationships. An RL finger-control policy produces executable rollouts, while the arm tracks precomputed trajectories. Rendered observations and recorded actions from successful rollouts are paired with grasp descriptions to fine-tune a VLA. Experiments show improved contact fidelity in retargeting and more reliable whole-arm execution than the evaluated baselines. Simulation evaluation and real-world deployment further demonstrate that a VLA fine-tuned solely on the generated demonstrations can execute language-specified grasps. Project page: this https URL .

title: LaST0.5: A Generalist World Action Model with Interaction-Centric Latent Reasoning
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, endowing policies with strong capabilities for modeling temporal and physical dynamics. Existing WAMs, encompassing both video-first action prediction and joint video-action modeling, directly transfer global physical representations from world models to action generation. However, global scene representations may underemphasize local robot-object interactions, creating a mismatch between representations optimized for world evolution and those required for manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose LaST0.5, a novel WAM that introduces an interaction-centric physical representation between world modeling and action generation. Specifically, LaST0.5 learns a compact interaction-centric latent space under the supervision of visual interaction cues between the robot and the environment. This reasoning space is instantiated as a latent expert that bridges the world expert and the action expert within a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture. Furthermore, LaST0.5 performs adaptive world-to-action transfer by jointly predicting future representations and progress values, using progress consistency to adjust action execution and trigger future resampling. Finally, we pretrain LaST0.5 on a large-scale robotic data corpus comprising over 14k hours of data, establishing interaction-centric physical reasoning as a scalable and effective paradigm. LaST0.5 achieves 99.5% on LIBERO, surpasses the previous state of the art on ten evaluated RLBench tasks, and demonstrates robust long-horizon execution and precise dexterous manipulation in real-world experiments.

title: WAM is capable in BEHAVIOR-1K: the 2nd-place solution to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge

summary: This work presents the 2nd-place solution (Team IF1001) to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge, which evaluates mobile manipulation across 100 household tasks. Our method is built on a powerful world action model (WAM), Cosmos 3. We improve Cosmos 3 by using richer visual history, task-progress conditioning, and task-group and skill-specific LoRA adapters. During inference, we apply a separate progress estimator to supply task-progress context, and use task- and progress-conditioned routing to select a task-group or skill-specific policy, complemented by action-candidate aggregation, rolling inpainting, and task-specific temporal and gripper control. To meet the minimum inference requirement of 1 FPS, we use neither recursive self-improvement (RSI) nor agentic harness methods and rely on no closed-source models; during official private-test evaluation, our system handled concurrent requests across 100 evaluation ports with limited hardware resources, sustaining an average end-to-end inference rate above 2 FPS per port. Our method achieves a mean Q-score of 0.613 and a full-task success rate of 40.9%, averaged over 3 self-evaluation rounds across all 100 tasks. On the official private test set, with 20 instances per task, our system achieves a mean Q-score of 0.615 and a full-task success rate of 41.2%.

title: From Depth to Safe Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Monocular Perception for Mobile Robot Navigation
summary: Monocular depth foundation models make it tempting to replace depth sensors on mobile robots with a single RGB camera. We show that, used off the shelf, this is unsafe: in a simulated indoor navigation benchmark, a standard Nav2 stack driven by Depth Anything V2 (metric) collides in 63\% of 120 episodes, because the model systematically over-estimates the distance to nearby obstacles. We propose a lightweight plug-in module that turns predicted depth into \emph{safe depth}. A 0.58\,M-parameter head on top of the \emph{frozen} depth model predicts, per pixel, a log-depth correction $\mu$ and an uncertainty $\sigma$, trained with a $\beta$-weighted Gaussian negative log-likelihood. The navigation stack consumes the one-sided bound $\hat d_{\text{safe}}=d\,e^{\mu-k\sigma}$, where $k$ is set by conformal calibration on a held-out world, and uncertainty also decides which pixels may be treated as floor. The correction halves the depth error (AbsRel $0.262\rightarrow0.134$) and reduces near-range over-estimation from 59.8\% to 12.0\%. In navigation, safe depth raises the success rate from 37\% to 70\% and lowers collisions from 63\% to 3\%, close to the 2\% of ground-truth depth. A constant safety margin calibrated to the same pixel coverage reaches only 30\% success because it freezes the robot; uncertainty-aware safety wins 52 of 56 discordant paired episodes against it. Gains hold on glass, texture-less walls and dark regions.

AI.tldr: 直接用现成单目深度基础模型（Depth Anything V2 度量深度）驱动 Nav2，在仿真室内导航中 120 个回合有 63% 发生碰撞，原因是模型系统性高估近处障碍距离。作者在冻结深度模型上加 0.58 M 参数头预测逐像素对数深度修正与不确定度，输出安全深度下界，使碰撞降至 3%、成功率由 37% 升至 70%。

title: From Prediction to Action: Learning Physical Context for Deformable Linear Object Manipulation

summary: A representation that accurately predicts a deformable object's response is not necessarily the one most useful for choosing manipulation actions. We study this distinction between predictive utility and decision utility in planar single-grasp shape control of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs). As a common decision backbone, we introduce Geometry-Pointer-Flow (GPF), a geometry-grounded policy that separates grasp-location selection from grasp-conditioned motion generation. Its geometry-only variant reduces one-step executed shape error by 32.8% relative to a DLO-specific diffusion policy, while using 18.7 times fewer parameters and achieving approximately 193 times faster inference. On this backbone, we compare physical context represented by ground-truth parameters, estimated parameters, and learned interaction-history representations, for both forward prediction and executed control. For prediction, ground-truth physical parameters reduce next-shape error by 15.8% over geometry alone, and estimated parameters are slightly more predictive than interaction history. This ordering does not carry over to control: estimated parameters provide no detectable one-step control gain, whereas history-conditioned GPF reduces executed error by 9.9% relative to geometry-only GPF across 470 paired simulation trials. In closed loop, interaction history improves strict-threshold attainment in simulation and yields the strongest zero-shot performance on hardware. All policies are trained exclusively in simulation and transferred to the physical robot without real-world training or fine-tuning. These results show that physical context should be evaluated by the decisions it supports rather than by predictive accuracy alone. Code will be released upon acceptance.

title: Elastic-WAM: Adaptive Spatiotemporal Imagination for Efficient Robot Control

summary: World-Action Models improve robot control by predicting future visual dynamics, but iterative video denoising incurs substantial inference overhead. Recent approaches reduce this cost through partial future denoising, yet typically rely on fixed refinement budgets. Our empirical observations reveal that preferred refinement depths vary across tasks and states, while different future regions exhibit varying relevance to action generation. Motivated by these findings, we propose Elastic-WAM, which adaptively allocates world refinement computation across temporal denoising time and spatial future space. A unified spatiotemporal refinement demand field governs when to stop world refinement, how far to advance each denoising step, and which regions to refresh. We parameterize this field with a shared temporal basis and spatial amplitudes, and learn it through a three-stage action-grounded supervised procedure. At inference, the learned field guides recurrent sparse world refinement to improve task success while reducing inference overhead. Evaluations across diverse simulation benchmarks and real-world long-horizon manipulation demonstrate state-of-the-art control performance with reduced inference latency.

title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge

summary: We describe our solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge: 100 long-horizon household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. We placed 9th on the final leaderboard, the only independent team in the top 10. The core of the solution is a single vision-language-action (VLA) model, one checkpoint for all 100 tasks, built on our 1st-place 2025 solution, which is based on $\pi_{0.5}$. On the 50 tasks shared with 2025, its Q rises from 0.260 to 0.371; across all 100 tasks it scores 0.392. Our main conclusion from 2025 was that the model was undertrained, so most of the 2026 work went into training the model for longer, optimizing some training parameters, making each training step slightly faster and reducing the gradient noise: a migration from 50 to 100 tasks (semantic stages built from the demonstrations' skill annotations, task and stage embeddings of new tasks warm-started from similar old ones, and a 21-dimensional action space matching the teleoperation controls); variance-reduced multi-sample flow matching with a simple noise-vs-compute model that picks the number of action-expert samples per observation without ablations; and a 200k-step training run, about one pass over the 211M frames of the demonstrations. A cloud evaluation infrastructure keeps a shared record with provenance, episode diagnostics and restorable simulator states, and runs six simulators on one GPU together faster than real time. On top of the learned policy, 14 tasks are routed to a GPT-6 Astra coding agent that controls the robot through observation and motion tools, starting every episode from a frozen copy of its own practice session on training instances. Across these 14 tasks, Astra's mean Q is 0.639, against 0.108 for the learned policy. The public submission included only part of the Astra results and scored 0.446 Q with 27.3% full-task success.

title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies

summary: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. Because time passes even when nothing happens, such a memory may not tell waiting from working. We show that it does not. On the counting tasks of RoboMME, we make the robot briefly pause or fidget its wrist. Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early. We call this failure phantom progress. It cuts success from 47 to 16 of 50 on one task and from 44 to 10 on the other. When the same frames are withheld from memory, success returns, so the cause lies in memory rather than in the interruption itself. We trace the failure to a temporal shortcut: because demonstrations proceed at a steady pace, elapsed time predicts progress. Indeed, rescaling the time stamps alone makes the policy stop early when the clock runs fast and repeat when it runs slow. Surprisingly, removing the time encoding does not cure the failure, because the frames of a null event still occupy slots of the time-sampled memory. Across RoboMME's released designs, vulnerability follows how memory is indexed. Of the fixes the diagnosis suggests, training with injected pauses does not remove the failure and impairs counting, whereas indexing memory by events recovers half or more of the loss without retraining. A memory meant to remember what happened should count events rather than clock ticks.

title: OnlyAct: Extracting Action Representations from Foundation Models for World Models
summary: Video world models promise general-purpose interactive simulators, but their training is limited by action supervision: action labels are scarce, fragmented across incompatible specifications, and do not scale with the unlabeled video pretraining corpus. A common workaround jointly trains an action encoder to compress consecutive frames into a latent action and a decoder to reconstruct the next frame from the previous frame and that latent, forcing the latent to capture only new information. This has two limitations: learning the action space from scratch can limit generalization to unseen domains, and the bottleneck trades expressiveness for separation, with tighter settings losing nuance and looser ones risking scene leakage under domain shifts. We argue for a different starting point: rather than learning actions from scratch, we start from a pretrained foundation model (V-JEPA 2), whose embeddings of a frame pair already carry substantial action information after large-scale, diverse video pretraining. The remaining challenge is to extract the action while discarding the scene. We propose a label-free contrastive adaptation framework that pulls together frame pairs sharing the same motion under a different scene and pushes apart pairs from the same scene with different motion, reshaping the geometry of the pretrained space without imposing a reconstruction bottleneck. We introduce a unified evaluation protocol along three axes (action expressiveness, scene invariance, and action-conditioned video generation quality) across robot manipulation, camera navigation, game, and driving benchmarks, most of which are unseen during adaptation. Compared with annotation-free latent-action methods, our representations are substantially more expressive while matching their scene invariance, and they yield world models that transfer demonstrated actions to new scenes more faithfully.

title: Building World Models from Intrinsic Motivation
comment: 27 pages, 11 figures
summary: In the absence of extrinsic rewards or task supervision, human behavior is guided by intrinsic motivation---neural signals that drive curiosity, creativity, play, and other essential facets of intelligence. Intrinsic motivation plays an important developmental role in building robust world models that enable generalization and adaptation. Yet existing studies leave open how a broad range of intrinsic motivations interacts with world-model representation learning to support downstream control. This limits our understanding of which intrinsically collected experiences build reusable models. To address these gaps, we integrate 24 intrinsic objectives, including established methods and explicit variants spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency, into a common model-based reinforcement learning framework. We evaluate the world models they build through zero-shot, few-shot, and multi-task control in locomotion, manipulation, and open-ended gaming environments, using three representation-learning strategies: observation reconstruction, latent prediction, and redundancy reduction. Curiosity-driven exploration with observation reconstruction yields the strongest aggregate family profile, although the best individual pairing depends on the experiment. In compositional vision-based tasks, intrinsic motivation derived from both episodic and lifelong novelty---providing a complementary memory to the world model's generic recurrent state---achieves the best zero-shot transfer and few-shot adaptation. These findings motivate designing intrinsic motivation and representation learning jointly. Our results demonstrate world models as a powerful tool for measuring the quality of intrinsically motivated experience, and positions intrinsic motivation as a key ingredient for building world models autonomously.

title: From Video Frames to Robot Meta-Frames: A Unified Latent Interface for World Action Models
summary: Pretrained video diffusion models (VDMs) offer a powerful foundation for World Action Models (WAMs), which jointly predict robot actions and future observations. Building such models requires injecting low-dimensional robot signals (e.g. proprioception, actions, and values) into a latent space shaped by natural videos, and a key design choice is the interface through which these signals enter: existing schemes treat it as a formatting detail, spending a separate latent frame on each signal or bolting on dedicated encoders and decoders. We argue that signal injection is instead a distribution-alignment problem: how well a representation matches the prior of the pretrained VDMs during denoising. Using the relative reconstruction error of a frozen VDM denoiser as a probe, we find that conventional spatial encodings sit far off this prior, whereas frequency-domain packing yields latents that the denoiser corrects far less. Motivated by this diagnostic result, we propose MetaWAM, which folds all robot signals into a single unified meta-frame: each signal is assigned to a disjoint frequency-domain channel band and lifted to the spatial latent by an inverse DCT, yielding a decodable interface aligned with the pretrained VDM prior without any added module or architectural change. A fixed band layout together with slot-aware routing lets the same meta-frame support policy, world-model, and value prediction over a shared set of robot variables. On RoboCasa, MetaWAM reaches 68.9% success while collapsing the per-signal frames into one and cutting inference latency by 39%, and attains 85.0% success on three real-world Franka tasks. title: Incorporating World Models in Decision Making for Next Best View Selection in Active Sensing
comment: Accepted to CoRL 2026 Workshop "Do Robots Need World Models?"
summary: Efficient robotic 3D reconstruction requires selecting views that contribute new surface measurements with few physical captures. Pretrained world models can guide this choice, but a predicted surface may not produce valid depth measurements under the operating conditions of the deployed sensor. We present a deployment adaptation methodology for next-best-view selection that learns a sensor-return adapter from limited local calibration data while keeping the pretrained predictor fixed. The adapter estimates measurement dropout over each predicted surface, allowing the selection method to favor views likely to fill gaps in the measured reconstruction. In a real-robot experiment with a structured-light sensor, the adapted method achieves higher measured surface coverage with 60% fewer captures than nominal selection. The adapted method recovers a surface region that the nominal method repeatedly targets but fails to measure. These results suggest that robots can reuse pretrained predictive models while adapting their decisions to local operating conditions in data-scarce environments.

title: Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics
comment: 33 pages, 8 Figures
summary: Effective search and rescue (SAR) operations require autonomous systems capable of coordinating multiple heterogeneous agents, adapting to dynamic hazards, and aligning with human mission intent. Existing language-guided reinforcement learning (RL) methods primarily focus on single-agent instruction following and lack mechanisms for team-level coordination in complex, partially observable environments. This paper presents a Cognitive Multi-Agent Framework based on Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (LG-HRL) that integrates natural-language understanding, hierarchical policy decomposition, and a shared cognitive workspace to achieve cohesive multi-agent behavior in SAR scenarios. Human instructions are interpreted by a large language model (LLM) and transformed into structured semantic cues that guide high-level strategy selection and role assignment across UAV and UGV agents. A formal Language-Grounded Multi-Agent Hierarchical Decision Process (LG-MAHDP) is introduced to model the interplay between semantic grounding, hierarchical control, and distributed coordination. Comprehensive experiments in a simulated disaster environment show that LG-HRL improves learning speed by 2.3 times, increases coordination coherence by 37%, and enhances subgoal accuracy and hazard avoidance by 46% and 31%, respectively. The system achieves 20-30% higher victim rescue rates, demonstrates emergent role specialization, and adapts immediately to human verbal updates. Ablation studies confirm that both the shared cognitive workspace and language grounding are critical to overall system performance. Overall, this work establishes a new paradigm for language-guided multi-agent SAR robotics, demonstrating that semantic grounding combined with hierarchical reasoning enables safer, more efficient, and more interpretable autonomous rescue operations.

title: CAFE: Closed-Loop Autonomous Task Formulation and Execution without Instance-Specific Instructions
summary: Scene-driven robot autonomy requires selecting tasks from observations as well as executing them. We study scene-driven task formulation and execution under predefined cleaning, safety, and storage/organization categories, without instance-specific goals or action sequences. CAFE maintains online memory of objects, functional zones, and execution states. A rule-guided Trigger-LLM admits formulation from accumulated evidence; Draft, Complete, and Audit propose goals, resolve execution details, and check dependencies. Outcomes update memory for correction and subsequent discovery. Evaluation in 12 AI2-THOR scenes compares three backbones and task-complexity tiers using coverage, constraint, and execution metrics. Tri-LLM records higher GCR scores than the evaluated baselines across three backbones and task-complexity tiers. Controls examine completion, auditing, zones, feedback, triggering, and prompt examples. LimoCobot traces illustrate storage, cleanup, and recovery from a failed grasp. The study examines how shared scene state connects task discovery to execution and outcome-driven revision.

title: APS-VLA: Action-Guided and Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have demonstrated strong generalization in robotic manipulation, yet processing dense visual tokens often incurs high inference latency. Visual token pruning offers a practical way to reduce this cost, but identifying a compact set of tokens that preserves reliable action generation remains challenging. Existing methods largely rely on static or immediate heuristic cues to estimate token importance. We introduce APS-VLA, a framework that learns visual token selection from robot demonstrations while keeping the pretrained VLA backbone frozen. A lightweight Decision Influence Estimator scores tokens conditioned on current visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioception. Its training combines two complementary signals: action supervision matches both the full-input policy predictions and demonstrated actions, while an auxiliary visual transition objective uses demonstrated actions to predict subsequent visual features from the selected representation. At deployment, the estimator performs a single hard selection and packing step before the policy's native action-generation procedure; the auxiliary predictor is removed. Experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO and with $\pi_{0.5}$ and XR-1 on RoboCasa365 demonstrate inference acceleration with modest changes in task success. Across five real-world tasks on two dual-arm platforms, APS-VLA reduces mean policy inference latency from 137.25 to 93.25 ms, achieving a $1.47\times$ speedup with an average success rate of 61%, compared with 60% for the unpruned baseline. Together, these results support APS-VLA as a modular, plug-in framework for efficient robotic control across VLA architectures, preserving the underlying policy parameters and native action-generation procedure.

title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
summary: Embodied Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are backbones for robotic planning and manipulation. However, for coordinate prediction in grounding tasks, existing architectures suffer from two distinct bottlenecks: discrete tokenization disrupts spatial continuity with high decoding latency, while standard point regression fails on multi-contact affordances and irregularly shaped targets. To resolve these challenges, we propose PhysMoE, introducing three core contributions: (1) sharing lower layers for multimodal context while routing upper layers to specialized spatial (pixel) and linguistic (text) experts by physical modality, eliminating gradient interference; (2) encoding each coordinate as a single token by reusing the visual encoder's learned positional embeddings, injecting 2D spatial priors to natively align coordinates with visual features and ease training; and (3) differentiable Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision on pointing, accommodating affordances and irregular geometries without costly mask decoders. Compared to the base model, PhysMoE achieves a 15.7% average gain and an 8.31x throughput speedup across 9 coordinate-based grounding benchmarks (trajectory, affordance, and localization), while preserving multimodal understanding and reasoning across 11 text-based embodied benchmarks.

AI.motivation: 具身 VLM 是机器人规划与操作的骨干，但其坐标预测存在两个明确瓶颈：离散 token 化破坏空间连续性并带来高解码延迟；标准点回归在多接触可供性（affordance）和不规则形状目标上失效。摘要据此提出需要同时改善空间连续性与几何适应性。

title: A computational framework for understanding embodied plans
summary: Reasoning about people's plans and goals based on their actions is fundamental to human social interaction and essential for cooperative, embodied artificial intelligence. Formalizing this capacity in naturalistic, embodied settings has been a longstanding challenge. Here, we present GenEA, a novel agent representation capable of reasoning over multi-step, long-horizon embodied plans. At the heart of GenEA lies a multilevel state-space that couples the coarse biomechanics of an articulated body and its interactions with nearby objects by extending the task-and-motion planning framework from robotics with simulation-based intuitive physics. By embedding this state-space in a generative model, GenEA yields a joint probability distribution over goals and embodied plans. Across several experiments spanning the qualitatively distinct domains of object manipulation and navigation, featuring diverse tasks and multiple behavioral measures, we show that GenEA, through simple transformations of this joint distribution, recapitulates how humans reason about embodied plans. Crucially, GenEA consistently outperforms strong alternative models, including plausible heuristics, standard task-and-motion planning, and a state-of-the-art vision-language model. GenEA thereby offers a new perspective on the architecture of human reasoning and social cognition, suggesting that embodied artificial intelligence systems seeking to seamlessly interact with humans should adopt GenEA-like generative models of action planning.

title: Curie's Jarvis: Autonomous Robotic Chemistry Experiments from Printed Protocols
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Rumi Loghmani and Bozhang Song contributed equally
summary: A person running a bench experiment works from a printed instruction sheet, tells identical containers apart by the labels written on them, and looks at the bench again before each step. Lab automation usually works the other way around: the procedure is written as a script, and containers stand at fixed positions or carry fiducial markers. We present Curie's Jarvis, a system that lets a robot arm carry out a chemistry experiment on a bench set up for people. It reads the steps from a photo of the printed sheet, finds containers on an ordinary bench with no fixed positions or markers, tells identical-looking containers apart by reading their labels in four camera views, locates its target again before every step, and sets how each step is carried out, including its speed, from what is being handled. title: Game-Enhanced Embodied Learning with Event and Foresight Pretraining

summary: Human gameplay supplies paired observations, actions, and visual consequences that can supplement robot-policy training. We study event-and-foresight pretraining for InternVLA-A1.5, combining recorded keyboard/mouse event prediction with history-conditioned visual supervision through a frozen video model. Coverage-preserving anchor selection constructs one-second targets, and an attention mask prevents teacher-forced future actions from entering foresight queries. The selected corpus contains 394 recordings across 20 games, with 223.36 hours of recorded timestamp span and 2,072,084 training anchors. After 12,400 game-pretraining updates, we compare the resulting initialization with the public base under the same suite-specific robot fine-tuning protocol. Across four LIBERO suites, aggregate success increases from 1,718/2,000 (85.90%) to 1,811/2,000 (90.55%), a gain of 4.65 percentage points. Suite gains are 9.2, 6.8, 0.2, and 2.4 points on Spatial, Object, Goal, and Long. The 40-task breakdown shows 24 improvements, 10 declines, and six ties. These results support the practical value of the complete game-pretraining stage in this evaluated setting, while revealing heterogeneous task outcomes. The comparison includes additional optimization and does not isolate the effects of game data, the two objectives, or training variability.

AI.tldr: 在InternVLA-A1.5上做“事件预测+基于冻结视频模型的前瞻视觉监督”的游戏预训练，再用同一套机器人微调协议评测；LIBERO四个套件聚合成功率从85.90%升到90.55%（+4.65个百分点）。
AI.motivation: 人类游戏过程自带“观测—动作—视觉后果”配对数据，可作为机器人策略训练的补充数据来源。摘要指出该工作的动机是研究这类游戏数据上的事件与前瞻预训练能否提供更好的策略初始化。

title: Camera equalisation of an 11.5x drop in environmental illuminance: four imitation-learning policies on an SO-101 arm
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, 8 tables. Data and code: this https URL
summary: Real-robot benchmarks of learned visuomotor policies often record room illuminance as the lighting condition. We show that, on a typical low-cost rig, room light and image light can be almost unrelated. Four imitation-learning policies (ACT, SmolVLA, Diffusion Policy and pi0.5) were trained on the same 50 demonstrations of a pick-and-place task on an SO-101 arm. Each was run for ten rollouts at about 520 lux and again at about 45 lux, an 11.5x reduction. Success was 20/40 in normal light and 19/40 in low light: a change of -2.5 percentage points (95% CI -23 to +19), with no evidence that the policies differed in sensitivity (interaction p = 0.86). The recorded video shows why: mean image brightness was only 3% lower in low light on the front camera and 19% lower on the wrist camera. Both cameras were set to automatic exposure and white balance, which most likely absorbed the difference; exposure was not locked in this experiment. An accidental repeat of one 10-rollout block reproduced its success count (7/10) but matched the first block at only 6 of 10 placements, consistent with chance. We conclude that lux alone does not describe what a policy sees. Camera settings, and image statistics compared with the training recordings, are the quantities to report and control. Data and code are public.

AI.tldr: 作者用真实 SO-101 机械臂上的抓取放置任务检验：房间照度从约 520 lux 降到约 45 lux（11.5 倍）时，四个模仿学习策略成功率仅从 20/40 变为 19/40（-2.5 个百分点）。原因是自动曝光/白平衡大幅吸收了光照差异，说明 lux 不能代表策略实际看到的图像。
AI.motivation: 真实机器人基准常把"房间照度"当作光照条件来记录，但作者指出在典型低成本装置上，房间光与图像光可以几乎无关，因此仅报告 lux 无法描述策略真正接收到的输入。
AI.method: 输入：真实 SO-101 机械臂上的抓取放置任务，四个模仿学习策略（ACT、SmolVLA、Diffusion Policy、pi0.5）使用完全相同的 50 条示教示范训练。做法不是改动策略算法，而是让每个策略在两种环境照度（约 520 lux 与约 45 lux）下各执行 10 次 rollout，比较成功率并做策略×光照的交互检验；同时从录像中测量两个摄像头的图像亮度统计，以观察相机链路实际传导了多少光照变化。输出：跨策略的成功率差异、敏感度交互结果，以及前摄像头与腕部摄像头的亮度变化幅度。
AI.result: 作者报告：正常光下成功 20/40，低光下 19/40，变化 -2.5 个百分点（95% CI -23 到 +19），交互检验 p = 0.86，无证据表明策略间敏感度不同。录像显示低光下前摄像头平均图像亮度仅低 3%，腕部摄像头低 19%，两摄像头均为自动曝光与白平衡。一次意外的 10 次 rollout 区块重复复现了成功次数 7/10，但与首个区块仅在 10 次放置中 6 次位置一致，作者称与随机相符。摘要未给出各策略单独成功率、实际 lux 测量不确定度等更细数值。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的评测实践而言，本文的提示是：报告与控制的量应是相机设置以及与训练录像可比的图像统计量，而非单个 lux 值。证据边界很窄——四个策略、单任务、单装置、每条件合计 40 次 rollout，置信区间宽（-23 到 +19 个百分点），且曝光未锁定，因此结论只支持"本装置上 lux 与策略所见图像几乎无关"，不足以推广为所有视觉运动策略对光照具有鲁棒性。
AI.core_method: 在同一 SO-101 装置与同一批 50 条示范上，让四个模仿学习策略分别在约 520 lux 与约 45 lux 下各跑 10 次 rollout，并用录像图像亮度统计检验相机对光照的实际传导。

title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
summary: Foundation models such as GPT and Claude have shown strong capabilities in spatial understanding and embodied intelligence. These advances make agentic robotics a promising path toward artificial general intelligence in robotics. However, we find that using foundation models to control robots poses serious safety risks, and comprehensive safety evaluation is still lacking. We introduce RoboRisk, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating safety in agentic robotics. Its 92 simulated tasks and 13 physical-robot tasks fall into five categories: Task-level Refusal (T), Plan Repair (P), Execution-time Hazard (E), Injection (I), and Sequential Memory (S). Prior benchmarks cover at most two of these categories, and several evaluate only text outputs. In contrast, RoboRisk covers all five and executes every task in closed loop. We evaluate six state-of-the-art foundation models on RoboRisk: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, and Grok 4.7. These models generally show high harm rates. We also evaluate two robot-specific APIs: the Dream API and PokeBot's RoboAPI. We further propose the Lease-Enforced Agentic Safety Harness (LEASH), which offers essential safety infrastructure for agentic robotics and can be integrated into nearly any agentic architecture. LEASH leverages a decision model (Jev or OpenAI's Decisions API) to implement task, action, and commit gates, which review the task, each action, and each irreversible operation in their visual context. The planner and all three gates share a common safety policy. Experiments on RoboRisk in simulation and on physical robots show that LEASH effectively reduces harm across all six foundation models. It largely preserves their task completion performance and adds little time and token overhead.

AI.tldr: 基础模型直接控制机器人存在安全风险，且缺乏覆盖全面的安全评测。作者提出 RoboRisk 基准（92 个仿真任务 + 13 个真机任务，五大类、闭环执行）并发现六个基础模型危害率高，进而提出 LEASH 安全框架（任务/动作/提交三道闸门，共享同一安全策略），在仿真与真机实验中降低危害且基本保持任务完成度、开销较小（摘要未给出具体数值）。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出：用基础模型控制机器人存在"serious safety risks"，而"comprehensive safety evaluation is still lacking"；已有基准最多覆盖五类风险中的两类，部分只评测文本输出。因此缺少覆盖全面、闭环执行的机器人智能体安全评测，也缺少可普遍接入的安全基础设施。
AI.method: 输入：机器人智能体任务，以及智能体在视觉上下文中的任务描述、每一步动作和不可逆操作。先构建评测侧 RoboRisk：92 个仿真任务与 13 个真机任务，分属 Task-level Refusal、Plan Repair、Execution-time Hazard、Injection、Sequential Memory 五类，每题闭环执行；用它对六个基础模型和两个机器人专用 API（Dream API、PokeBot 的 RoboAPI）做安全评测。方法侧提出 LEASH：借助决策模型（Jev 或 OpenAI 的 Decisions API）实现 task、action、commit 三道闸门，分别在视觉上下文中审查任务、每个动作、每个不可逆操作；规划器与三道闸门共享同一份安全策略。相对仅评测文本输出或最多覆盖两类风险的既有基准，变化在于全五类覆盖、闭环执行，以及把安全检查做成可接入"nearly any agentic architecture"的通用组件；产出为安全判定/拦截与任务执行结果。
AI.result: 作者报告：六个基础模型（GPT-6 Astra、GPT-6.1 Sol、GPT-6 Luna、Claude Opus 5.5、Gemini 4 Argon、Grok 4.7）在 RoboRisk 上普遍危害率高；LEASH 在仿真与真机实验中于全部六个模型上降低危害，并大致保持任务完成表现，时间与 token 开销很小。以上均为方向性定性结论，摘要未报告任何数值（无危害率、任务完成率、开销的具体取值），也未报告统计显著性；关于 Dream API 与 RoboAPI 的评测结果摘要未报告具体结论。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的意义是：把"安全"从单点过滤扩展为可评测的五类风险维度（拒绝、计划修复、执行期危险、注入、时序记忆），并把安全检查做成与规划器共享策略、可插入任意智能体架构的闸门机制，且同时覆盖仿真与真机。证据边界：全部结论均为作者自述，摘要只给出定性方向和少量比较性表述（如"Prior benchmarks cover at most two of these categories"），没有数值化结果、逐类别得分、消融、开销量化或与前人安全方法的定量对比，因此无法判断改进幅度、泛化到其他模型或硬件的程度。

title: Latent Barrier Steering: Hierarchical Safety for Generative Planning
summary: We introduce Latent Barrier Steering (LBS), a hierarchical semantic-to-path framework for safe flow-matching-based generative planning. Existing control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filters for diffusion and flow-matching planners act locally on generated samples, either during sampling or after prediction. Such repair is effective for small violations, but can struggle when a new constraint blocks the whole selected behavior mode rather than merely perturbing it locally. LBS decouples behavior selection from path certification through two coordinated interventions: it first steers the generator's behavior latent toward rollouts with larger safety margin, then decodes the steered latent and applies a path-space CBF quadratic program (QP) only for residual violations. We show that latent steering increases the margin available to the path-space corrector, yielding finite-time recovery guarantees and reduced correction burden. Experiments across navigation and robot end-effector planning tasks show that LBS preserves safety while improving goal reaching and reducing correction burden compared with path-level safety filters.

AI.tldr: LBS 把生成式规划的安全保障拆成两级：先在行为隐空间把生成器推向安全余量更大的行为模式，再用路径空间 CBF 二次规划（QP）修补残余违规。作者报告在导航与机械臂末端执行器规划任务中，LBS 在保持安全的同时改善到达目标并减轻修正负担。
AI.motivation: 现有面向扩散／流匹配规划器的控制屏障函数（CBF）安全过滤器只在生成样本上做局部作用——要么在采样过程中，要么在预测完成之后。这种修补对小幅违规有效，但当新约束是整体阻断所选的整个行为模式、而非仅局部扰动它时，就容易失效。
AI.method: 输入是流匹配（flow-matching）生成式规划器的行为隐变量与安全约束。方法与既有路径级安全过滤器不同之处在于把“行为选择”与“路径认证”解耦，分两步干预：第一步在隐空间将生成器的行为隐变量朝安全余量更大的 rollout 方向引导；第二步解码被引导后的隐变量，仅对残余违规施加路径空间的 CBF 二次规划（QP）修正。输出是既满足安全约束、又完成目标到达的规划路径。作者称隐空间引导为路径空间修正器留出了更大余量，从而给出有限时间恢复保证并降低修正负担。

title: RedirectMimic: Local Motion Content Redaction for Humanoid Whole-Body Control

summary: Humanoid motion interfaces should accommodate application-specific movement constraints while retaining useful reference behavior. Local content redaction requires a controller to replace selected movements even when it continues to receive the original reference. Removing the tracking incentive for those movements leaves their replacement unspecified. We introduce RedirectMimic, which separates the reference observed by the actor from the target used to train its execution. A rule-generated edited reference guides tracking rewards during proximal policy optimization, while the deployed observation and action interfaces remain unchanged. We evaluate pose- and speed-defined arm editing in Unitree G1 simulation using a tracker pretrained on 7,509 motion clips. On the overhead-arm task, RedirectMimic reduces core-window content occurrence to 2.7%, compared with 58.9% for reward zeroing and 32.8% for anti-tracking. It achieves 94.2% core-window joint success, combining content suppression, fall-free execution, and local retention. On the speed-defined task, fast outward arm movements occurred at similarly low rates under all three local editing methods. Across both tasks, RedirectMimic achieved the lowest replacement error among these methods and tracked unedited motions with accuracy comparable to that of the pretrained controller. summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models now exceed 95% success on the LIBERO simulation benchmark, yet it remains unclear how much of this performance requires generalization beyond the training demonstrations. title: Koopman Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
summary: We propose a Koopman model-based reinforcement learning (K-MBRL) algorithm for controlling nonlinear robotic systems with unknown dynamics. The K-MBRL learns a control policy by minimizing an approximate policy objective that combines the analytical immediate cost with an estimate of the future cost evaluated at the one-step predicted state. To this end, we develop a stochastic Koopman operator-based learning method to approximate the unknown nonlinear dynamics in a linear representation, while a critic function estimates the remaining future cost. This formulation offers two key advantages. First, the linear Koopman dynamics simplify the model-dependent policy gradient computation to a constant matrix product, enabling computationally efficient policy improvement. Second, one-step model propagation mitigates the accumulation of prediction errors associated with long-horizon rollouts while retaining long-term cost information through the critic. The learned policy enables real-time control through feedforward evaluation without online optimization. We establish policy learning convergence guarantees under standard stochastic approximation assumptions. Simulations on HalfCheetah and quadruped four-legged locomotion tasks demonstrate strong sample efficiency and improved performance compared with classical model-free and model-based reinforcement learning baselines. A pendulum swing-up task is used to assess policy gradient approximation accuracy and conduct ablation studies on the learning mechanism and key hyperparameters. The proposed K-MBRL is further validated on a physical quadruped robot performing a challenging sequence of maneuvers: rising to an upright posture supported by two rounded rear feet, maintaining balance during bipedal walking, and safely returning to the ground, as shown in Fig.1.

title: Force-Closure Condition for Cooperative Multi-robot Pushing of Rectangular Objects
comment: 7 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Published in CAOS 2026
summary: In cooperative object manipulation, the placement of pushing contacts determines whether force closure can be achieved and agents can generate arbitrary forces and torques on the object correspondingly. This study derives a necessary and sufficient closed-form condition for the planar force closure of a rectangular object, a common object shape in everyday settings, under four frictionless pushing contacts. For a rectangle of length $b$ and width $a$, force closure holds if and only if $(l_1+l_3-b)(l_2+l_4-a)<0$, where $l_1,l_2,l_3,l_4$ are the four edge contact locations. This condition is independent of the object's center of mass and is used to verify contact configurations before contact force allocation. When the condition is not satisfied, the signs of the two factors indicate which opposing contact pair should be adjusted. The condition and adjustment rule are then integrated into a full-pose trajectory-tracking framework as a geometric feasibility layer to demonstrate their use in control. Static wrench feasibility tests validate the proposed condition, while narrow-passage floating-body simulations show that maintaining a force-closure configuration reduces the RMS tracking errors in $x$, $y$, and unwrapped yaw from $12.05$ m, $18.11$ m, and $535.96^\circ$ to $2.24$ m, $2.66$ m, and $2.69^\circ$, respectively.

title: One Trajectory, Two Requirements: Accuracy and Local Stability in Euler Sampling for Flow Matching Policies
summary: Flow matching robot policies commonly use a fixed Euler step count selected from offline accuracy sweeps. At inference time, however, each policy input (visual observation, robot state, and language instruction) together with a source-noise draw defines a different ODE trajectory and sequence of local Jacobians. We ask whether a step count that accurately follows the nominal noise-to-action trajectory can still be too coarse for strongly contracting directions around it. An exact two-coordinate system and a controlled augmentation of six trained flow models show that trajectory accuracy and local Euler stability can impose different step requirements even when the original learned transport is unchanged. We then study a frozen $\pi_{0.5}$-LIBERO checkpoint without modifying its weights or action dynamics. Across 30 policy inputs from 10 LIBERO-10 tasks, the Jacobian exhibits strong contracting directions near the action endpoint, yet no sampled mode violates the Euler non-expansion condition. On five of those inputs, accuracy sweeps require 4--9 Euler steps at 5% terminal error and 87--112 at 1%. These five paired cases are therefore consistent with accuracy-limited rather than stability-limited sampling under this local criterion, while the controlled experiments show why endpoint accuracy alone cannot rule out a separate stability requirement.

AI.tldr: Flow matching 机器人策略的 Euler 步数通常由离线精度扫描固定，但每个策略输入加噪声采样都对应不同的 ODE 轨迹与局部 Jacobian。作者用局部非扩张条件检验采样稳定性：在冻结的 π_0.5-LIBERO 检查点的 30 个输入上未发现违反该条件的模式，而其中 5 个输入的精度扫描需 4--9 步（5% 终端误差）。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出步数取自离线精度扫描，而推理时每个策略输入（视觉观测、机器人状态、语言指令）配合一次源噪声采样，都会定义不同的 ODE 轨迹与局部 Jacobian 序列；因此尚不清楚"能准确跟随名义噪声到动作轨迹"的步数，是否对轨迹周围的强收缩方向仍然过粗。
AI.method: 输入是 flow matching 策略的采样过程：每个（视觉观测、机器人状态、语言指令）加一次源噪声决定一条噪声到动作的 ODE 轨迹。方法不修改已学习的传输映射，而是做两件事：一是构造一个精确的两坐标系统，并对六个已训练 flow 模型做受控增广，用同一学习传输比较"轨迹精度"与"局部 Euler 稳定性"各自提出的步数要求；二是冻结一个 π_0.5-LIBERO 检查点（不改权重与动作动力学），沿轨迹取局部 Jacobian 检查 Euler 非扩张条件，并做终端误差精度扫描。输出是两类需求对应的步数，以及各输入属于精度受限还是稳定性受限的判断。

title: A human-in-the-loop Control Paradigm for Construction Robotics: From VR-Guided Teleoperation to Semi-Autonomous Dual-Arm Operation
comment: under review
summary: Construction tasks in hazardous and unstructured environments require both human adaptability and robotic precision, yet existing approaches often treat teleoperation and autonomy as separate control modes. This paper presents a human-in-the-loop control paradigm that enables structured transitions among VR-guided teleoperation, semi-autonomous shared control, and rule-based autonomous execution for contact-rich dual-arm construction tasks. The proposed system combines immersive VR guidance, a manually defined library of reusable skill primitives, and a shared-autonomy framework with explicit human-robot role allocation and command-priority rules. This integration allows operators to retain supervisory and corrective authority while delegating repetitive and precision-critical actions to the robot. The paradigm is validated on a dual-arm platform through representative facade-installation tasks. Results show that autonomous execution provides the best performance under well-calibrated nominal conditions, whereas semi-autonomous control improves resilience when environmental disturbances exceed the predefined autonomous pipeline's correction capability. Semi-autonomous control also substantially reduces subjective operator workload compared with full teleoperation. These findings demonstrate that effective construction-robot control should adapt human involvement to task and environmental uncertainty, using autonomy for repeatable operations and shared control for disturbance recovery.

title: AHEADance: Anticipatory Humanoid Dance from Streaming Audio
summary: A humanoid that dances to streamed music must commit each motion chunk before it has heard the music that chunk accompanies, and must continue from motion it has already committed. We present AHEADance, a robot-native streaming dance generator executed on a humanoid robot by a whole-body tracker. ListenAhead conditions each chunk on heard music and a frozen music model's forecasts of the coming music, aligned to their target times and weighted by reliability. The forecasts carry the timing of upcoming beats almost as well as the actual future; with them, the generator is better synchronized with the music and concentrates more motion energy at its song's beat frequency. Commit Forcing trains continuation from the model's own committed chunks, updating both the latent history and the decoded boundary of the next chunk; it reduces low activity from 83.5% to 10.3%, the level of real dance. Three music evaluators, each validated on real G1 dance, test synchronization, song and style. On a physical Unitree G1, it dances while the music plays and comes to rest when it stops, without a fall. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: 流式音乐下的人形机器人舞蹈必须在听到对应音乐前就提交每个动作块，并从已提交动作继续。AHEADance 用 ListenAhead（以已听音乐 + 冻结音乐模型对未来音乐的预测为条件）与 Commit Forcing（从自身已提交动作块训练续接）实现机器人原生流式舞蹈生成，在实体 Unitree G1 上边放音乐边跳、音乐停止即停下且未摔倒。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出的核心矛盾是：随流式音乐跳舞的人形机器人必须在尚未听到该动作块所配音乐时就提交动作，并且必须从已经提交的动作继续下去。
AI.method: 输入是流式音频与机器人已提交的动作历史；输出是逐块生成、并由全身跟踪器在实体人形机器人上执行的动作。相对既有做法的改变有两处：ListenAhead 让每个动作块同时以「已听到的音乐」和「一个冻结音乐模型对即将到来音乐的预测」为条件，预测按目标时间对齐并按可靠性加权；Commit Forcing 则让模型从自己已提交的动作块出发训练续接，同时更新潜变量历史与下一动作块的解码边界。

title: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable
comment: Accepted by DAI 2026
summary: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. However, existing SDLs exhibit a fundamental paradox: foundation model integration has increased linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding. By treating models as disembodied planners that output symbolic workflows for separate robotic systems, current architectures inherently block the development of embodied experimental intuition. We argue that overcoming this paradox requires embedding \emph{learnability} along three interdependent axes: cognitive learnability (learning what to investigate), experimental learnability (learning where to search), and embodied learnability (learning how to act). Building on this view, we introduce the Embodied Science Agent (ESA), which unifies digital intelligence with physical embodiment through three synergistic components: a Digital Agent that provides cognitive and experimental learnability via memory-based reasoning and Bayesian optimisation, an Embodied Agent that provides embodied learnability via generalisable instrument control, and an Embodied Unified Interface for seamless coordination. We validated ESA in autonomous wastewater treatment experiments, navigating over 200 million possible conditions. Through 15 continuous rounds, ESA raised the final solution transmittance from 82\% to 99.7\%, corresponding to a 98.5\% reduction in residual dye concentration and near-complete decolourisation, while its learned visuomotor policies generalised across varying instrument placements, a promising step toward next-generation SDLs for autonomous scientific discovery.

AI.tldr: 现有自驱动实验室（SDL）把基础模型当作离身规划器、输出符号工作流交给独立机器人系统，语言能力提升但物理接地被切断。作者提出 Embodied Science Agent（ESA），用数字智能体、具身智能体与统一接口把认知/实验/具身三种可学习性耦合起来；在自主废水处理实验中经 15 轮连续实验把最终溶液透过率从 82% 提升到 99.7%，并报告残留染料浓度下降 98.5%。

title: DOBB: Dynamic Oriented Bounding Boxes for Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance under State Uncertainty and Heterogeneous Dynamics
summary: Learning-based decentralized collision avoidance must remain reliable under state-estimation uncertainty and heterogeneous agent dynamics. Existing methods typically address these factors through training-domain variation or by exposing uncertainty and capability estimates to the policy at runtime. However, both leave the policy to infer how these quantities should alter the physical separation required for safe interaction, which can couple collision-avoidance behavior to relationships learned from the training distribution. We introduce the Dynamic Oriented Bounding Box (DOBB), an online geometric representation that maps the current state estimate, uncertainty, and agent-specific response characteristics into a dynamic, direction-dependent safety margin. We derive geometric features that jointly characterize the relative configuration and severity of interactions between agents' DOBBs, along with a reward function that preserves the physical interpretation of those interactions. Across four evaluation environments, DOBB achieves the lowest mean total failure rate of 2.6%. This performance persists under out-of-distribution shifts in actuation dynamics and state-estimation uncertainty, with collision-based failure remaining at or below 2.3% in every tested condition. We attribute this robustness to the geometric abstraction of the safety margin, which is less coupled to the specific uncertainty and actuation regimes encountered during training.

AI.tldr: DOBB 用在线几何表示把状态估计、不确定性与各智能体响应特性映射为方向相关的动态安全边界，在多智能体去中心化避碰中取得四项环境中最低的平均总失败率 2.6%，并在分布外扰动下保持碰撞类失败 ≤2.3%。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出，学习式去中心化避碰必须在状态估计不确定与智能体动力学异质的情况下保持可靠；已有方法要么靠训练域变化，要么把不确定性/能力估计直接暴露给运行时策略，二者都把"这些量应如何改变安全交互所需的物理间距"留给策略自行推断，从而使避碰行为与训练分布中学到的关系相耦合。
AI.method: 输入是当前状态估计、其不确定性以及智能体自身的响应特性；DOBB 是一个在线几何表示，把这些输入映射为随方向变化的动态安全裕度，即动态有向包围盒。方法进一步推导几何特征，用来联合刻画各智能体 DOBB 之间的相对构型与交互严重程度，并设计一个保持这些交互物理含义的奖励函数。输出是供策略使用的几何化安全表示与相应奖励信号，使安全裕度不再依赖训练中见到的特定不确定性与驱动条件。相对基线（训练域变化或向策略暴露不确定性估计的既有方法），其改变在于把安全间距显式几何化，而不是让策略从数据中推断。

AI.conclusion: 对具身智能中多智能体避碰而言，该工作提示：把不确定性与异质动力学显式转成几何安全边界，可能比让策略隐式学习更易泛化到分布外条件。但证据仅限摘要报告的失败率数字，未报告基线数值、环境类型（仿真/真机）与统计细节，因此不能推断实际部署表现或相对提升幅度。

title: RiSE-Drive: Risk-Sensitive Long-Horizon Candidate Evaluation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
comment: 11 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables, including supplementary material. Published in ACM Multimedia 2026 (MM '26)
summary: End-to-end autonomous driving systems increasingly rely on generating multiple trajectory candidates and selecting one for execution. In this setting, a central challenge is no longer only candidate generation, but how to evaluate candidates according to their long-horizon consequences under uncertainty. Existing methods still mainly use deterministic point scores, heuristic subscores, or single-outcome evaluations, which makes it difficult to capture delayed failures, tail risk, and ranking instability under plausible future perturbations. We present RiSE-Drive, a framework for risk-sensitive long-horizon candidate evaluation in end-to-end autonomous driving. RiSE-Drive first performs candidate-conditioned latent future rollout, then estimates long-horizon outcome distributions instead of single scalar scores, and finally ranks candidates using a tail-risk-aware and perturbation-robust decision criterion. This reformulates candidate scoring from deterministic oracle-style evaluation into distributional outcome assessment with explicit risk control. title: Gaussian Process-Augmented Model Predictive Contouring Control for 6-DoF Trajectory Tracking with a Holonomic AUV

summary: Small, holonomic Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) enable close-range inspection of underwater structures from arbitrary viewpoints, requiring accurate position and attitude tracking under state and input constraints. title: Maze Runner: Autonomous Maze Navigation with Line-Based Localization and Control Barrier Functions
comment: 10 pages, 8 figures, 1 table. Code: this https URL
summary: Maze navigation requires localization from sparse, repetitive geometry, planning through narrow corridors, and control that stays safe when the estimate or the map is wrong. We present Maze Runner, an open autonomy stack in C++ and ROS 2 that addresses these needs end to end on a simulated Husarion ROSbot XL with a 2D LiDAR in Gazebo. Perception extracts wall lines from each scan with RANSAC and total least squares, with per-line uncertainty. The same line front end feeds two estimators: an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) that localizes against a line map built from the maze mesh, and an EKF SLAM variant that builds the line map online. Planning runs online on an inflated occupancy grid with A* plus line-of-sight shortcutting, or with a forward-only Hybrid A*. A nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC) tracks the plan while discrete-time Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) on world-frame LiDAR points keep the robot clear of walls and unmapped obstacles. The algorithms live in a ROS-free, unit-tested core library, and the whole stack builds and runs from a single reproducible environment. In simulation, the robot drives a 135 m route through the maze with 1.0 cm localization RMSE against the known map and 24 cm in SLAM mode, the planner returns a path in 6 ms, and the NMPC solves in 11.7 ms on average, never exceeding its 80 ms budget.

title: Route-Time Conflict Maps for Cooperative End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: Existing cooperative end-to-end driving works at Class A (status-sharing) of the SAE J3216 classes of cooperative driving automation (CDA): vehicles exchange what they perceive, not what they intend, so each plans alone when to go, which limits cooperation and leads to deadlock when both vehicles yield or to collisions when both go. We present When2Go, a cooperative end-to-end driving system that learns when to go by sharing intent under CDA Class B or higher. Each vehicle broadcasts its LiDAR detections with forecast motion as instance tokens, together with its plan and intended trajectory. The receiver draws the fused detections, forecasts and partner plans into a route-time conflict map, the occupancy along its route over the planning horizon, on which a planner scores candidate speed profiles. Where two intended trajectories conflict, an order gate, a precedence network distilled from a right-of-way rule, decides who goes first; both vehicles evaluate it on the same messages and so reach the same order. When2Go imitates the rule-based expert of V2Xverse, which sees the simulator's ground truth; stops that When2Go cannot observe within its 2 s planning horizon are relabelled, so that it does not learn to wait without an observable cause. For our runs only, the benchmarks' PID controller steers by When2Go's waypoints instead of the route, and its forced push of long-waiting vehicles is off. With one model, When2Go sets the state of the art on three closed-loop CARLA benchmarks: 97.8 and 90.7 driving score on InterDrive without and with traffic (best published 90.1 and 78.9), 70.0 on the public V2Xverse protocol (best of sixteen rerun methods 59.1) and 88.2 on MDrive (best rerun 85.1), with 95.0% of its vehicles collision-free (87.7%).

AI.tldr: 现有协作式端到端驾驶停在 CDA Class A（只交换感知、不交换意图），车辆各自决定何时通行，双方都让行会死锁、都抢行会碰撞。When2Go 改为在 Class B 及以上共享意图，把融合后的检测、预测与伙伴计划写成"路线-时间冲突地图"，在候选速度上打分，并用由路权规则蒸馏出的先后门控决定谁先走；作者报告其在三个闭环 CARLA 基准上取得最优成绩。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出的具体缺口是：Class A 的状态共享只让车辆交换"看到什么"而非"打算做什么"，因此每辆车独自决定何时通行，合作受限；两车都让行时死锁，都走时碰撞。
AI.method: 输入：每辆车广播其带预测运动的 LiDAR 检测（作为实例 token），以及自身计划和意图轨迹。接收方把这些融合的检测、预测与伙伴计划汇成"路线-时间冲突地图"，即在规划时域上沿自身路线的占据情况；规划器据此为候选速度剖面打分。当两条意图轨迹冲突时，一个由路权规则蒸馏得到的先后门控（precedence network）判定谁先行，双方基于相同消息评估、因而得到相同顺序。训练上模仿 V2Xverse 中能看到模拟器真值的规则专家，并把 When2Go 在 2 s 规划时域内观察不到的停车重新标注，以免学到没有可观察原因的等待。输出：被下游规划/控制使用的航点（其运行中 PID 控制器改为跟踪 When2Go 的航点）。相对既有协作式端到端工作的改变是从状态共享升到意图共享，并在同一模型内完成冲突判定。

AI.conclusion: 对具身智能的意义在于：把协作驾驶的瓶颈从"共享感知"推进到"共享意图+冲突消解"，用可解释的路线-时间占据表示与路权规则蒸馏的先后门控，让多车在同一消息上得到一致的通行顺序，并以单一模型覆盖多个闭环基准。证据边界明确：全部为 CARLA 仿真闭环结果，摘要未报告实车验证；且作者说明其为自己的运行修改了基准协议（PID 改为跟踪 When2Go 航点、关闭对长时间等待车辆的强制推动），因此与公开协议的对比条件并不完全等同，摘要也未报告延迟、模型规模或消融。

title: ForeseeDrive: Future-Token Conditioning for Anticipatory Generative Driving
comment: 15 pages (8 pages main text + appendix), 3 figures, 7 tables
summary: Generative driving planners can represent diverse ego futures, but a downstream scorer can choose only among sampled candidates; it cannot recover an absent maneuver. We present ForeseeDrive, which turns future scene evolution into a deployable interface for shaping candidate generation. Rather than reconstructing dense future states or scoring a fixed menu, ForeseeDrive derives query-indexed tokens from logged actor motion, occupancy evolution, route interactions, and TTC margins, and predicts the same token space from present context at deployment. The tokens condition trajectory geometry before candidates materialize. A zero-token-gated residual path and candidate-preservation loss limit unnecessary drift, while a TTC-margin guard targets brittle safe-to-unsafe boundary crossings. Under their respective benchmark protocols, ForeseeDrive reaches 89.2 PDMS on NAVSIM navtest, 0.41\,m average L2 and 0.05\% collision rate on nuScenes validation, and a 76.50 driving score on Bench2Drive. Controlled DiffusionDrive/NAVSIM diagnostics show an exact zero-token no-op, a small aligned-over-shuffled selected-PDM advantage under preservation, mixed oracle-best quality, and localized TTC-boundary failures. Together, the benchmark results and bounded mechanism tests support future-conditioned generation as a practical interface for anticipation. Code is included in the supplementary materials.

AI.tldr: ForeseeDrive 把“未来场景演化”编码成可从当前上下文预测的 token，用其生成条件约束轨迹采样，而非只在已采样候选中挑选。作者报告 NAVSIM navtest 上 89.2 PDMS、nuScenes 验证集平均 L2 0.41 m 与 0.05% 碰撞率、Bench2Drive 驾驶分 76.50。
AI.motivation: 摘要指出的具体缺陷是：生成式驾驶规划器虽能表达多样的自车未来，但下游打分器只能在已采样候选中选择，无法找回“没有被采样到的机动”（cannot recover an absent maneuver）。因此需要一个能提前影响候选生成、而不是事后筛选的接口。
AI.method: 输入侧：从日志中的他车运动、占据演化、路线交互与 TTC 余量中导出按查询索引的 token；部署时改为从当前上下文预测同一 token 空间。机制：这些 token 在候选轨迹真正生成之前就对其几何形状施加条件，即把未来场景演化变成“塑造生成”的可用接口，而不是重建稠密未来状态或对固定候选清单打分。为限制不必要的漂移，加入零-token 门控的残差路径与候选保持损失；另设 TTC 余量护栏，针对“安全→不安全”边界附近的脆弱穿越。输出：条件化后的候选轨迹。
AI.result: 作者报告：在其各自的基准协议下，NAVSIM navtest 达 89.2 PDMS，nuScenes 验证集平均 L2 为 0.41 m、碰撞率 0.05%，Bench2Drive 驾驶分为 76.50。机制诊断（DiffusionDrive/NAVSIM 受控实验）显示：零-token 时精确无操作（no-op）；在保持约束下，对齐 token 相对打乱 token 仅有小幅的 selected-PDM 优势；oracle-best 质量表现混合；TTC 边界失败呈局部化。摘要未给出与具体基线方法的数值对比，因而这些数值的相对强弱无法从摘要判断。
AI.conclusion: 对具身智能/世界模型读者的意义：它把“预测未来”用作生成策略的先验接口——未来 token 不是被重建的状态，而是提前约束轨迹几何的条件信号，从而在采样之前改变候选分布。证据边界：全部为作者自述结果，且摘要只给出各基准的绝对数值，未报告基线比较、样本量、统计显著性、硬件或延迟；诊断实验的结论被作者自己限定为“bounded mechanism tests”。
AI.core_method: 从日志未来演化提取 query-indexed token，并训练模型仅由当前上下文预测该 token 空间，用预测 token 在候选生成前条件化轨迹几何，辅以零-token 门控残差与 TTC 余量护栏。
